'''Douglas A. Mitchell''' is a professor of chemistry at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. He holds an affiliate appointment in the Department of Microbiology and is a faculty member of the [[Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology]].<ref name=uiuc>{{cite web|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/Douglas_Mitchell.html|title=Douglas A. Mitchell - Chemistry at Illinois|website=www.chemistry.illinois.edu|accessdate=5 August 2017}}</ref> His research focuses on the [[chemical biology]] of [[natural products]]. He is known mainly for his work on the biosynthetic enzymology of [[ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides]] (RiPPs) and genome-guided natural product discovery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=arWBqN8AAAAJ&hl=en|title=Douglas A Mitchell - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|accessdate=5 August 2017}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Mitchell was born in western Pennsylvania and obtained his B.S. in chemistry from [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 2002. He obtained his PhD in 2006 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and worked with [[Michael Marletta]] on the [[nitric oxide]]-dependent [[post-translational modification]]s of proteins. For postdoctoral studies, he worked with Jack Dixon at the [[University of California, San Diego]] and pursued the study of Streptococcal toxin biosynthesis. In 2009, he began his independent career at the  [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] as an assistant professor of chemistry. In 2015, he was promoted to associate professor with tenure.

==Research interests==
* [[Natural products]]
* Genome-mining
* [[Antibiotic resistance]]
* Mechanistic enzymology
